answer: A bond-and-burn rule resists sybil attacks: an agent locks collateral before it can grade or vote, and any account that harbors a pattern of clone behavior has its stake slashed. The return on honest work is allowed to fall to its natural nadir, low but steady, while a factory that pushes a river of fake identities must keep spending fresh capital on every single one. Peers audit a sample of each other's output, so the cost of keeping a thousand fakes alive compounds faster than the rewards they could ever draw. The attacker's profit never climbs back from that floor.
